newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio state to appeal Banerj injunction -- report.
newsitem.headline: Rio state to appeal Banerj injunction -- report.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state government will appeal a court injunction which suspends the privatization auction of Rio state bank Banerj scheduled for Tuesday, a local news agency said.
Invest News said the legal team of the state privatization program was preparing an appeal against the injunction granted by Rio state judge Ronald Pietri at the request of a bank employees union.

The union questioned Banerj's tender documents regarding the bank's pension and payroll-related debts. Under the tender details, Rio de Janeiro state would assume all of Banerj's debts to its pension fund, which would be covered by a federal loan.
The judge has ordered Rio state to publish new tender details wihtout the item concerning the debts being assumed by the state.
Banerj was scheduled to be privatized in a closed-envelope auction Tuesday at 1400 local time/1700 GMT on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange.
But the sale of Banerj, the first Brazilian state bank to be privatized, also depends on Senate approval of the 2.9 billion real loan to cover the pension-related debts.
The state failed to sell the bank last year due to worries over its debts and the possibility of injunctions against the sale. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
